proposals.evidence: CDIAL 11392 sense 2 explicitly compares Old Marwari barasa, Hindi baras and Gujarati varas 'year'. The survey's baras/baraś/varaś agree in their vowel-broken r-sibilant cluster; use the year sense, not the rain sense. The single varś record is deferred because its retained cluster may reflect learned influence.

11392 varṣá n. 'rain' RV., pl. 'the Rains' AV. 2. 'year ŚBr. [√vr̥ṣ]   
1. Pa. vassa- m.n. 'rain', pl. 'the Rains', Pk. vāsa- m. (or < vārṣa-), varisa- m.n., Wg. waṣ, Kt. wōṣ m. Dm. baṣ,
Paš.nir. dar. weg. wāṣ, lagh. wāx̌, Niṅg. baṣ, Shum.
wāṣ, Woṭ. baš, Kaṭ. baṣ, Gmb. waṣíṅ, Gaw. wā̆ṣ,

Kal. cmpd. before v- > b-), Sv. baṣ, Phal. bā̆ṣ m.; K.
wośᵘ m. 'light shower of rain'; WPah.bhal. bàri f. 'the
Rains'; Ku. bas-kāl 'a rainy season', B. barisā; Si. vas
'rain, the Rains', vaharē; Md. vārē 'rain'. — Dard.
forms, esp. those with -ā- may, like Kho. baṣ, be
< vārṣá-.   
2. Aś.shah. man. vaṣa-, kāl. dh. jau. vasa- 'year'
(these may, like gir. vāsa- be < vārṣá-), NiDoc. varṣa,
Pk. varisa- m.n., Gy. eur. berš m., pal. wars, as. vers,
Ḍ. bəris; Phal. bḗriṣ, bέriṣ 'summer' NOPhal 29, AO
xviii 228 (but if bḗriš, as in AO viii 300, then <
várṣya-); Sh. bărĭ́ṣ, pl. °ĭẓí m. 'year', K. warih, wahar
m., kash. warhiĕn obl. pl., ḍoḍ. barīē, S. varhyu m., L.
varhā m., mult. varhẽ, awāṇ. vàrā, P. varah, varihā,
varhā, ba° m. (varas, ba° m. ← Centre), WPah.bhal.
bàri f., pāḍ. cam. barh, paṅ. barhā, N. barsa, A. barih,
B. baris, Or. barasa, Bhoj. baris, OAw. barisa m., H.
baras, barsā m., OMarw. barasa m., OG. vāse loc. sg.
m., G. varas n., Si. vas-a, vā SigGr ii 462.   
várṣya-, vārṣá-, vā́rṣika-; varṣakāla-, varṣartu-,
*varṣāgra-, *varṣāyaṇa-, *varṣāhaṇa-, *varṣōdaka-,
*varṣōdaya-; *antarvarṣa-, *kuhavarṣa-, trivarṣa-,
*navavarṣa-, *saṁtatavarṣa-, saptavarṣa-.

(obl. -a) 'year'.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2402 section 1 compares Marwari ū̃ṛo and Gujarati ū̃ḍũ 'deep', with Bhalessi uṇḍe and Kumauni un 'down'. These support both the retroflex nasal-stop family and the positional sense 'below'; sections 2 *ōṇḍa- and 3 *avōṇḍa- are not the appropriate parents.
proposals.primaryEvidenceText:
2402 *ūṇḍa 'deep'. 2. *ōṇḍa-. 3. *avōṇḍa-.    1. Pk. uṁḍa-, °aya- 'deep', S. ūnho; WPah. bhal.
uṇḍe 'down'; Ku. uno 'low', un 'down', uniṇo 'to lower
(of clouds)'; H. poet. ū̃ṛā 'deep, sunk'; Marw. ū̃ṛo 'deep',
G. ū̃ḍũ.   
2. H. õḍā 'deep', M. õḍ, õḍhā, õḍhā.   
3. H. aũḍā, OMarw. aũṛo.   
ūta- see *ūna-².   
Addenda: *ūṇḍa-: S.kcch. ūno 'deep'.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8138 section 1 gives Prakrit pāhaṇa and Gujarati pāṇ, pāṇɔ 'stone'; its addendum adds Kachchi pāṇo. These closely support pāṇā. Turner explicitly leaves the early ṣ > h development unexplained, so it is a documented lexical history rather than an asserted general sound law.
proposals.primaryEvidenceText:
8138 pāṣāṇá 'stone' ṢaḍvBr. 2. pāṣāṇī- f. 'small stone used as a weight' lex. [Cf. pāṣī-. Early occurrence of -h- in Pk. and thence in NIA. (though in S. P. Si. -ṣ- regularly > -h-) is unexplained. Poss. connexion with
*pāhāḍa-]   
1. Pa. pāsāṇa-, °aka- m. 'stone, rock', Pk. pāsāṇa-,
pāhā̆ṇa- m.; S. pahaṇu m. 'stone', °ṇī f. 'pebble'; P.
pāhaṇ m. 'stone', Mth. pāhan, OAw. pāhana m., H.
pāhā̆n m., OG. pāhaṇiiṁ inst. sg. m., G. pāṇ, pahāṇɔ,
pāṇɔ m., Si. pahaṇa, pāṇa. — X śāna-.   
2. B. pāṣāṇ 'the excess of weight in one scale which
disturbs the equipoise'.   
Addenda: pāṣāṇá-: S.kcch. pāyaṇ, pāyṇo, pāṇo m. 'stone'.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 5656 gives Prakrit taṇū and Hindi tan 'body', providing an inherited comparison for the Jesingpura Malvi record tan. This is tanū́ 'body', not tanú 'thin' (5654). Persian tan is a possible contact influence; the isolated survey form cannot independently exclude borrowing, so the inherited analysis remains provisional pending review.
proposals.primaryEvidenceText:
5656 tanū́ f. 'body, person, self' RV., tanú- f. AitBr. [tán-]    Pa. tanu- n. 'body', Pk. taṇū- f.; Sh. (Lor.) tan 'body',
tan-nano 'naked'; K. tan (dat. °ni) f. 'body' (tonᵘ m.
'belly below the navel' rather < tunda-¹); P. taṇ, taṇā
m. 'side of belly'; N. tan-man 'with mind and body';
B. tanu 'body, skin'; H. tan m. 'body'; Si. tunuva 'body,
shape'.   
*tānuva-, tā́nva-; tanūjá-, tanūpā́-; *uttanuka-.
